module_title: Supreme Court of India - Basic Understanding
introduction: The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial court under the Constitution of India. It is the final court of appeal and the 'Guardian of the Constitution'. Articles 124 to 147 in Part V of the Constitution deal with the organization, independence, jurisdiction, and powers of the Supreme Court.

core_concepts.title: Establishment and Composition (Article 124)
core_concepts.description: The Supreme Court was inaugurated on January 28, 1950. At present, it consists of 34 judges (1 Chief Justice of India and 33 other judges). The power to increase the number of judges lies with the Parliament.

core_concepts.title: Appointment and Oath
core_concepts.description: Every judge of the Supreme Court is appointed by the President of India. The oath of office is also administered by the President or a person appointed by them.

core_concepts.title: Qualifications for Judges
core_concepts.description: To be a judge, a person must be: 1. A citizen of India. 2. A judge of a High Court for at least 5 years, OR an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, OR a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President.

core_concepts.title: Tenure and Retirement
core_concepts.description: A judge of the Supreme Court holds office until they attain the age of 65 years. They can resign by writing to the President.

important_entities.name: H.J. Kania
important_entities.significance: He presided over the first sitting of the Supreme Court of independent India.

important_entities.name: Fathima Beevi
important_entities.key_fact: First Female Judge of the SC
important_entities.significance: She was the first woman to be appointed to the Supreme Court (though no woman has been the CJI yet).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Unlike the President or MPs, the Constitution does NOT prescribe a minimum age for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Supreme is Senior (65), High is Junior (62)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Supreme Court judges retire at 65, while High Court judges retire at 62.

exam_strategy_tips: Who can increase the number of judges? Parliament. Who appoints them? The President. Don't flip these!
Remember that the SC succeeded the Federal Court of India established under the Government of India Act, 1935.
